title: Finite free continuous coefficient sheaves have invariant rank on a nonempty scheme
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ [def-pc-scheme], on its small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site] put $E_W=p_W^*\underline E$, where $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For $n\in\mathbf N$ let $E_W^{\oplus n}$ be the direct sum of $n$ copies of the regular $E_W$-module sheaf, with $E_W^{\oplus0}=0$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. If $|W|\ne\varnothing$ and $m,n\in\mathbf N$, an isomorphism $E_W^{\oplus m}\simeq E_W^{\oplus n}$ of $E_W$-module sheaves implies $m=n$. No quasi-compactness, connectedness, Noetherianity or invertibility of $\ell$ on $W$ is assumed.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6 (continuous-function realization on any scheme); elementary matrix evaluation and dimension comparison in the blueprint det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank proof, first paragraph

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] the topology on $E$ comes from a nonarchimedean absolute value. Its balls are clopen: if $y\notin B(a,r)$, the ball $B(y,|y-a|_E)$ misses $B(a,r)$ by the ultrametric inequality. For distinct $a,b$, a ball of radius $0<r\leq|a-b|_E$ separates them, so every connected subset of $E$ is a singleton. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization] with $T=E$, $X=W$. It gives a ring-sheaf isomorphism $E_W\simeq R$, where $R(U)=C(|U|,E)$, including multiplication and unit. Transport the given module isomorphism and its inverse along this ring-sheaf isomorphism; their composite identities are retained by conjugation. It suffices to consider $f:R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}$ and $g:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus m}$ with $gf=1$, $fg=1$.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6: pulled-back condensed coefficients are continuous-function sheaves; specialization using nonarchimedean clopen balls

proof.text: For $F_r=R^{\oplus r}$ denote the coproduct inclusions by $i_j:R\to F_r$. Define $p_j:F_r\to R$ by $p_ji_k=\delta_{jk}1_R$ using the coproduct universal property. Module morphisms, as defined in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], add pointwise; the map $\sum_j i_jp_j$ becomes $i_k$ after precomposition with every $i_k$, hence equals $1_{F_r}$. Thus these are biproduct coordinates, as in [def-weil-additive-category]. When $r=0$, the empty sum is the zero object and its identity is zero. All sums here are finite; no preservation of infinite coproducts by sections is used.

source.place: First paragraph: transition isomorphisms preserve the finite free rank; explicit matrix-evaluation argument

proof.text: For a regular-module endomorphism $h:R\to R$, its map on sections over $W$ is $R(W)$-linear: evaluating the module-morphism action equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on $a\otimes b$ gives $h_W(ab)=a h_W(b)$. Hence $h_W(a)=a h_W(1)$. Put $A_{ij}=(p_i f i_j)_W(1)\in C(|W|,E)$ for $i<n,j<m$, and $B_{ji}=(p_j g i_i)_W(1)$ for $j<m,i<n$. Insert the finite identity resolutions from step 2 into $gf=1$ and $fg=1$. For example, the $(j,k)$ component of $gf$ evaluated at $1$ is $\sum_{i<n}h_{ji,W}(a_{ik,W}(1))=\sum_{i<n}A_{ik}B_{ji}$, where $h_{ji}=p_j g i_i$ and $a_{ik}=p_i f i_k$. Since $E$ is commutative, this says $BA=I_m$. The same calculation with $f,g$ interchanged gives $AB=I_n$.

source.place: First paragraph: transition isomorphisms preserve the finite free rank; explicit matrix-evaluation argument

proof.text: Choose $w\in|W|$, using the nonemptiness hypothesis. The map $C(|W|,E)\to E$, $a\mapsto a(w)$, preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ because these operations are pointwise. Evaluating every entry of $BA=I_m$ and $AB=I_n$ therefore gives $B(w)A(w)=I_m$ and $A(w)B(w)=I_n$. The formulas $v\mapsto A(w)v$ and $u\mapsto B(w)u$ consequently define mutually inverse $E$-linear maps $E^m\rightleftarrows E^n$. Empty-index matrices and empty sums obey the same formulas when $m$ or $n$ is zero.

source.place: First paragraph: transition isomorphisms preserve the finite free rank; explicit matrix-evaluation argument

proof.text: The standard coordinate vectors form a basis of $E^n$: $v=\sum_{i<n}v_i e_i$, and $\sum_i c_i e_i=0$ implies $c_i=0$ by taking the $i$th coordinate. Therefore $\dim_E E^n=n$ by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. The $m$ images under $A(w)$ of the coordinate vectors of $E^m$ are linearly independent: applying $B(w)$ to a zero linear combination recovers the original coordinate coefficients. Apply [lem-weil-independent-family-card-le-dimension] to get $m\leq n$. Interchanging $A(w)$ and $B(w)$ gives $n\leq m$, and antisymmetry gives $m=n$. Both inequalities remain valid for zero-dimensional spaces.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-6f4345455 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full and wrote no fixes. The delivery adds 0 new nodes; the statement, stmt_deps, source and unit are unchanged, there is no repair note for the item, and no SGA source is cited. Source check: HRS arXiv 2305.18131, Example 3.1, p. 6, says Λ_X = U ↦ Maps_cont(U,Λ) for any scheme X. Blueprint main-20261015 sk-lem-stratified-lattice-rank.proof.md, paragraph 1, says transition isomorphisms preserve rank because E_X(W)≠0. The item states exactly this comparison, with rank 0 included and no hypothesis weakened. Parent det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank steps 1–2 apply it on W = U_i×_X U_j, and the hypotheses match. Step 1: lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value makes |·|_E ultrametric, so balls are clopen and E is totally disconnected. lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization then gives an isomorphism of ring sheaves E_W ≅ C(|−|,E), and both inverse identities transport along it. That node is an accepted tool_use from unit sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors: it is only the coefficient bridge and is not supplied in this unit. The closure of the six proof_deps has 350 nodes and contains neither the item nor its parent, so there is no cycle. Step 2: the biproduct coordinates p_j i_k = δ and Σ i_j p_j = 1 are correct; adding module morphisms uses the module-morphism equation of sk-def-sfb-module-objects. Step 3: h_W(a) = a·h_W(1). I checked the indices (A is n×m, B is m×n); the (j,k) entry of gf at 1 is (BA)_jk, so BA = I_m and AB = I_n. Step 4: evaluation at w ∈ |W| is a ring homomorphism, so A(w) and B(w) are mutually inverse; no claim about field stalks is used. Step 5: the coordinate basis gives dim E^n = n, the images of the basis under A(w) are independent, and the card-le-dimension node gives m ≤ n and, by symmetry, n ≤ m. Edge cases: m=0<n forces I_n = 0, which is impossible; W = ∅ shows the nonemptiness hypothesis is necessary; non-qc, disconnected and nonreduced W need no extra hypotheses. Duplicates: rg -L for invariant-basis and rank phrasings found only ordinary field, ring or scheme statements, none for continuous or condensed coefficient sheaves.
